name: app_metrics_installs_history
description: An app's total installs worldwide, at most one point per day (days without data are absent), with `daily` — the gain per day since the previous point (null on a first point with no earlier data and on a day the total fell). For growth over the window, subtract the first `total` from the last. Worldwide only: there is no per-country figure. Google Play figures are Google's exact install count, and `total_bucket` is the range its store page shows. Apple publishes no install counts, so App Store figures are an estimate: approximate for any single app, most reliable as a trend over time or between similar apps, and to be presented to the user as an estimate. Pick the window with `from` / `to`; the last 30 days by default. Costs 10 credits.

arguments.name: store
arguments.desc: Which app store: "android" (Google Play) or "ios" (App Store).

arguments.name: package
arguments.desc: App package / bundle id, e.g. "com.discord" (Android) or a numeric App Store id. If you only have the app name, call app_search first to resolve it.

arguments.name: from
arguments.desc: First day, YYYY-MM-DD. 30 days before `to` by default.

arguments.name: to
arguments.desc: Last day, YYYY-MM-DD, not before `from`. Today by default.

name: app_metrics_revenue_worldwide
description: An app's estimated revenue from store purchases over the last 30 days: worldwide `gross` (what users paid) and `net` (what the developer keeps after the store's commission), each with a `low`–`high` range and a size `bucket`, plus the split by country, largest first. Neither store publishes revenue, so these are estimates on both stores: approximate for any single app, best for sizing an app or comparing apps, and to be presented to the user as estimates. An app the store lists no purchases for reads 0. Figures are in USD unless `currency` is given. Costs 10 credits.

arguments.name: store
arguments.desc: Which app store: "android" (Google Play) or "ios" (App Store).

arguments.name: package
arguments.desc: App package / bundle id, e.g. "com.discord" (Android) or a numeric App Store id. If you only have the app name, call app_search first to resolve it.

arguments.name: currency
arguments.desc: Currency of the figures, an ISO 4217 code such as "EUR" or "GBP". USD by default.

arguments.name: limit
arguments.desc: How many countries to return, up to 250. 50 by default.

name: app_reviews
description: Read real user reviews of an app: author, star rating, text and date, 40 per page. Use it to find out what users actually complain about or praise. On Google Play, page through in order (1, 2, 3…) while `has_more` is true, each page within about an hour of the previous one and with the same sort_type; skipping ahead fails with PAGE_EXPIRED (not charged), so start again from page 1. The App Store serves a single page: there is no page 2 on ios. Costs 4 credits.

arguments.name: store
arguments.desc: Which app store: "android" (Google Play) or "ios" (App Store).

arguments.desc: Only reviews with this star rating.

arguments.name: sort_type
arguments.desc: Review sort order: 0 most relevant, 1 most recent (default), 3 top rated.

arguments.name: page
arguments.desc: Page number, 1 by default. Only the page after the last one read (within about an hour, same sort_type) works; Google Play only.
